preserved_failed_attempts.error: Processor image rebuilt to a different ID despite unchanged application sources; all ACK histories replayed, but processor replacement failed no-disruption assertion. Original before/after inspections retained.

Initial down prototype removed the container without persisting its current processing identity; up defaulted to empty demonstration topics. Order histories retained and replayed. Restore from saved inspection, then qualify fixed down/up.

Prototype shutdown guard required exit zero; both Connect JVMs exited SIGTERM status 143 after current-incarnation Kafka Connect stopped messages. No OOM or SIGKILL. Teardown stopped before deleting resources. Native logs and original stopped inspection retained; corrected guard requires native completion and rejects exit 137.

Connect native completion passed; Kafka brokers cleanly stopped with exit 143 but prototype checked an obsolete completion string. Corrected against pinned BrokerServer and KafkaRaftServer source. No resource deletion occurred. Original retry log and stopped inspections retained.

compression_scope: CRC32C-checked full source/output partition segment copies on one in-sync replica; record sections only, headers/indexes/RF3 separately. All twelve partition directories covered.

resources.limits: Cgroup CPU across all threads; one core = 100%. Memory mean is a sample mean; maxima are sampled charged/anonymous usage, not process peak RSS or simultaneous stack peak. Block I/O is runtime cgroup accounting, not logical engine I/O; empty counters are unavailable. I/O latency/queue depth unavailable. Stopped tails and short-lived work can be missed. Host controllers/Docker VM overhead excluded.

host_controller.limits: Controller CPU deltas include witness reconciliation; child CPU is local CLI processes, not Docker VM/container work. Peak RSS is process-lifetime and can include earlier trials in the same invocation, not a per-trial or whole-stack peak. Docker daemon/VM overhead excluded.

measurement_limits: Container resource counters cover the baseline, native probes and initial full replay, not image builds, later lifecycle replays or teardown.
CPU sums observed container deltas; memory is sampled charged/anonymous memory, not a simultaneous stack peak or process heap. Host controller counters are separate.
Block bytes are partial coverage as enumerated; missing counters are unknown. Runtime API did not expose IOPS, I/O latency or queue depth.
Writers stopped during lifecycle maintenance; retained replay establishes persistence, not continuous availability. No cache controls: these are buffered/recent-data observations.
Core fault cases and three diagnostic trials were qualified separately before this lifecycle pass; the single aggregate invocation and extended matrix remain unrun.
